function.name: calculate_electric_current
function.description: Calculate the electric current through a conductor given voltage and resistance. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

voltage.description: The voltage across the conductor in Volts. This is a float type value.

resistance.description: The resistance of the conductor in Ohms. This is a float type value.

conductance.description: The conductance of the conductor in Siemens. Optional if resistance is provided. Default: 0.3 This is a float type value.

message.content: Electricity was not “discovered” by a single person; it has been known and studied by many cultures and scientists over millennia. The earliest recorded observations of static electricity date back to ancient Greece (e.g., Thales of Miletus in the 6th century BCE). The modern scientific study of electricity began in the 17th and 18th centuries, with key figures such as William Gilbert, Otto von Guericke, and especially Benjamin Franklin, who coined the term “electricity” and conducted famous experiments with lightning. Subsequent discoveries by scientists like Alessandro Volta, André-Marie Ampère, Michael Faraday, and James Clerk Maxwell built the foundation of our modern understanding of electric phenomena.
